title: Rabbi Berekhyah son of Rabbi Simon, Grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: So it is cited in Otzar Yisrael from Kohelet Rabbah 10:7, but Hyman charges it with false testimony: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi never had a grandson named Rabbi Berekhyah; he had only one grandson, named Rabbi Mayasha. And what is cited in Yuchasin HaShalem, “Rabbi Berekhyah son of Rabbi Simon, son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,” Hyman calls an error and proposes “Rabbi Berekhyah son of Rabbi Simon,” and afterward it cites “son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,” etc., and the two entries were joined together.

notes.text: The accusation, claimed absence of a grandson named Berekhyah, single-grandson assertion and proposed joining of entries are Hyman’s bibliographical/genealogical argument. The heading represents the claim he disputes; it is not an independently admitted genealogy.

Otzar Yisrael III, printed page 210, directly prints the compounded genealogy “Berekhyah son of Simon, son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi” and cites the Kohelet Rabbah story on “There is an evil I have seen.” The consulted digital Kohelet Rabbah 10:5 has an unnamed son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. Hyman’s supplied 10:7 is retained; his denial and proposed joining of Yuchasin entries remain his argument, not an independently established genealogy.
